ORDER
The above matter comes on for entry of a final order of disposition by the Oklahoma Tax
Commission. Having reviewed the files and records herein, the Commission hereby adopts the
Findings of Fact, Conclusions of Law and Recommendation made and entered by the
Administrative Law Judge on the 3rd day of May, 2024, appended hereto, together herewith shall
constitute the Order of the Commission.
SO ORDERED
FINDINGS OF FACT, CONCLUSIONS OF LAW AND RECOMMENDATION
NOW on this 3rd day of May 2024, the above-styled and numbered cause comes on
for decision under assignment made by the Oklahoma Tax Commission (“Tax
Commission”) to ALJ2, Administrative Law Judge. COMPANY (“Protestant”) appears
through counsel, ATTORNEY. The Audit Services Division ("Division"), formerly the
Compliance Division, of the Oklahoma Tax Commission, appears through SAGC, Senior
Assistant General Counsel, and AGC, Assistant General Counsel, Office of the General
Counsel, Oklahoma Tax Commission.
STATEMENT OF THE CASE
By letter dated May 21, 2020, the Division proposed an adjustment to Protestant’s
2017 Consolidated Oklahoma Corporation Income Tax Return (“2017 Return”). The
Division proposed to disallow net operating loss carryover deductions for losses
generated by AFFILIATED COMPANY.1 for the 2015 and 2016 tax years on Protestant’s
2017 Return. Protestant was granted an extension until September 21, 2020, to file its
protest. By letter dated August 12, 2020, Protestant timely protested the adjustment.
On September 16, 2020, the Office of Administrative Law Judges received the
above-styled protest file for proceedings consistent with the Uniform Tax Procedure
Code2 and the Rules of Practice and Procedure Before the Office of Administrative Law
Judges.3 The case was assigned to ALJ1, Administrative Law Judge, and docketed as case
1 AFFILIATED COMPANY is part of the affiliated group of corporations included in Protestant’s 2017 Return.
2 68 O.S.2011, § 201 et seq., as amended.
3 Rules 710:1-5-20 through 710:1-5-49 of the Oklahoma Administrative Code ("OAC") govern proceedings related
to tax protests.
1 of 20 OTC ORDER NO. 2024-06-04-15

NON-PRECEDENTIAL DECISION OKLAHOMA TAX COMMISSION
number P-20-113-R.
On December 2, 2020, the Court entered a Prehearing Teleconference Notice
directing the parties to appear by telephone on December 10, 2020. The prehearing
teleconference was held as scheduled. The parties requested additional time to
communicate and to allow Division’s counsel to review additional information received
by the Division.
On February 22, 2021, the parties filed a Joint Proposed Scheduling Order
regarding discovery. On September 7, 2021, the parties filed a second Joint Proposed
Scheduling Order and agreed to submit the case on briefs.4 On September 17, 2021, the
parties filed Joint Stipulation of Facts, Issue, and Exhibits. On October 15, 2021,
Protestant filed Protestant’s Brief-in-Chief pursuant to the Scheduling Order filed in this
case. The Division filed its Response Brief of the Division on November 15, 2021.
Protestant filed Protestant’s Reply Brief on December 2, 2021.
On December 6, 2021, the Court closed the matter and submitted the case for decision.
On February 6, 2024, this protest was reassigned to ALJ2, Administrative Law Judge, and
renumbered P-20-113-SI.
FINDINGS OF FACT
JOINT STIPULATED FACTS AND EXHIBITS
On September 17, 2021, the parties filed Joint Stipulation of Facts, Issue, and Exhibits as
follows, to-wit:
STIPULATED STATEMENT OF THE ISSUE
Whether the Division properly disallowed Protestant’s use of Oklahoma net operating
losses generated by AFFILIATED COMPANY during the 2015 and 2016 tax years as claimed on
Protestant’s 2017 Form 512 Corporation Income Tax Return?
STIPULATED STATEMENT OF THE FACTS
1. Protestant acquired AFFILIATED COMPANY (“AFFILIATED COMPANY”) during the
2014 calendar year.
2. For the 2015, 2016, and 2017 tax years, Protestant and AFFILIATED COMPANY
(“AFFILIATED COMPANY”) were members of an affiliated group of corporations filing
consolidated federal corporate income tax returns.
5

3. AFFILIATED COMPANY filed separate Oklahoma corporate income tax returns for tax
years 2015 and 2016.
4. AFFILIATED COMPANY generated Oklahoma net operating losses in tax years 2015
and 2016.
5. On November 16, 2018, the Division received Protestant’s Form 512 Corporation Income
Tax Return for tax year 2017 (the “2017 Return”).
6. The Protestant made an election to file a consolidated corporate income tax return with the
filing of its 2017 Return on behalf of an affiliated group of corporations including AFFILIATED
COMPANY and several other entities.
7. The 2017 Return was Protestant’s first income tax filing in the state of Oklahoma.
8. The 2017 Return included net operating loss carryover deductions for Oklahoma net
operating losses generated by AFFILIATED COMPANY for tax years 2015 and 2016 totaling
$954,163.
9. The Division has not received any notice from the Internal Revenue Service of an
adjustment to the taxable income, as defined in the Internal Revenue Code, reported on the
Protestant’s 2017 federal consolidated corporate income tax return.
10. In a letter dated May 21, 2020, the Division adjusted Protestant’s 2017 Return.
11. The Division’s adjustments to the 2017 Return disallowed Protestant’s utilization of net
operating losses generated by AFFILIATED COMPANY during the 2015 and 2016 tax years.
12. In a letter dated July 16, 2020, the Division granted Protestant an extension of time to file
a protest to September 21, 2020.
13. Protestant timely protested the Division’s adjustment to the 2017 Return in a letter dated
August 12, 2020 (the “Protest Letter”).
14. Protestant’s protest is properly before the Administrative Law Judge.

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
WHEREFORE, premises considered, the undersigned concludes as a matter of law:
Jurisdiction, Notice, Burden of Proof and Agency Rules:
1. Jurisdiction of the parties and subject matter of this proceeding is vested in
the Tax Commission. 68 O.S.2011, § 221.
2. In administrative proceedings before the Tax Commission, the burden of proof is
on the taxpayer to show in what respect the action or proposed action of the Tax Commission is
incorrect. OAC 710:1-5-47; Enterprise Management Consultants, Inc. v. State ex rel. Okla. Tax
Comm’n, 1988 OK 91, ¶ 5, 768 P.2d 359, 362; Geoffrey, Inc. v. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 2006 OK CIV
APP 27, ¶ 25, 132 P.3d 632, 640 (citations omitted). The burden of proof standard is
“preponderance of evidence.” 2 Am.Jur.2d Administrative Law § 344. Each element of the claim
must be supported by reliable, probative, and substantial evidence of sufficient quality and quantity
as to show the existence of the facts supporting the claim are more probable than their
nonexistence. Id. Failure to provide evidence showing the action of the Tax Commission is
incorrect will result in denial of the protest. OAC 710:1-5-47.
3. An order of the Tax Commission must be supported by substantial evidence.
Dugger v. State ex rel. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 1992 OK 105, ¶ 9, 834 P.2d 964, 968 (citations
omitted). Likewise, the audit upon which a portion of the record is formed, and an order is issued,
must be supported by substantial evidence. An audit is supported by substantial evidence when an
evidentiary foundation for the audit has been established. Usually, the evidentiary foundation will
6 of 20 OTC ORDER NO. 2024-06-04-15

NON-PRECEDENTIAL DECISION OKLAHOMA TAX COMMISSION
be established by the records reviewed by the auditor. Where an evidentiary foundation has been
established, the taxpayer must prove the action of the Tax Commission is incorrect, and in what
respect. Failure to provide evidence showing the action of the Tax Commission is incorrect will
result in denial of the protest. OAC 710:1-5-47; Enterprise, supra.
4. Rules promulgated pursuant to the provisions of the Administrative Procedures
Act8 are presumed to be valid until declared otherwise by a district court of this state or the
Oklahoma Supreme Court. 75 O.S.2011, § 306(C).
5. In interpreting a statute, the fundamental rule and primary goal is to ascertain and
give effect to legislative intent. Rogers v. Quiktrip Corp., 2010 OK 3, ¶ 11, 230 P.3d 853, 859, as
revised (Feb. 4, 2010), as revised (Mar. 8, 2010) (footnote omitted). “The law-making body is
presumed to have expressed its intent in a statute’s language and to have intended what the text
expresses.” Blitz U.S.A., Inc. v. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 2003 OK 50, ¶ 14, 75 P.3d 883, 888, as
corrected (May 22, 2003) (footnote omitted). Therefore, the starting point for any inquiry into
legislative intent is the language of the statute. Blitz, 2003 OK 50, ¶ 14. “[W]here a statute is plain
and unambiguous, it will not be subject to judicial construction, but will be given the effect its
language dictates.” Id.
Income Tax, Consolidated Returns, and Net Operating Loss:
6. The Oklahoma Income Tax Act (“Act”)9 imposes income tax upon the Oklahoma
Taxable Income of every resident or non-resident who earns income within Oklahoma.
68 O.S.Supp.2014, § 2355.
7. “Taxation is an exclusively legislative function that can be exercised only under
statutory authority and in the manner specified by statute.” State, ex rel. Okla. Tax Comm’n v.
Texaco Expl. & Prod., Inc., 2005 OK 52, ¶ 7, 131 P.3d 705, 707. Accordingly, the basis for
assessing income tax must be found in the Act.
8. Income tax liability is determined according to the laws in effect at the time the
income is earned. Affiliated Mgmt. Corp. v. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 1977 OK 183, 570 P.2d 335;
Wootten v. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 1935 OK 54, ¶ 10, 170 Okla. 584, 40 P.2d 672, 674.
9. For the 2017 tax year at issue, Oklahoma imposed an income tax of six percent
(6%) upon the Oklahoma Taxable Income of corporations doing business within Oklahoma or
deriving income from sources within Oklahoma. 68 O.S.Supp.2014, § 2355(D).
10. “Oklahoma Taxable Income” means “taxable income” as reported (or as would
have been reported by the taxpayer had a return been filed) to the federal government, and in the
event of adjustments thereto by the federal government as finally ascertained under the Internal
Revenue Code, adjusted further as provided in the Act. 68 O.S.Supp.2013, § 2353(12).
8 75 O.S.2011, § 250 et seq., as amended.
9 68 O.S.2011, § 2351 et seq., as amended.

11. Any term used in the Act shall have the same meaning as when used in a
comparable context in the Internal Revenue Code (“IRC”) unless a different meaning is clearly
required. For all taxable periods covered by the Act, the tax status and all elections of all taxpayers
shall be the same for all purposes material hereto as they are for federal income tax purposes except
when the Act specifically provides otherwise. 68 O.S.Supp.2013, § 2353(3).
12. The starting point for computing Oklahoma taxable corporate income is the taxable
income shown before the net operating loss and special deduction line of the federal income tax
return. Federal taxable income is used for each separate corporation doing business in Oklahoma,
whether a consolidated Federal or a consolidated Oklahoma income tax return is filed. OAC
710:50-17-50.
13. All adjustments provided for under the Act are made from the starting point of
Federal Taxable Income (“Adjustments Rule”). OAC 710:50-17-51; See also 68 O.S.Supp.2016,
§ 2358.
14. An affiliated group of corporations may elect to file a federal consolidated return
in lieu of separate returns under the IRC. 26 U.S.C. § 1501 (2012).
15. The term “affiliated group” means “one or more chains of members connected
through ownership by a common parent entity if the common parent entity directly owns stock or
other equity interests meeting the requirements of Treas. Reg. 1.1471-5(i)(4) in at least one of the
other members (without applying the constructive ownership rules of section 318).”
FATCAHelp101 | Internal Revenue Service (irs.gov) (last visited May 1, 2024), See also
26 U.S.C.A. § 1504 (West 2014).
16. If two or more affiliated corporations file a consolidated federal return and if one
or more of the affiliated group earns a portion of its income from sources outside of Oklahoma,
the group is not required to file an Oklahoma consolidated income tax return. 68 O.S.2011,
§ 2367(2); See also OAC 710:50-17-31. However, the affiliated group may elect to file a
consolidated Oklahoma income tax return under such circumstances. 68 O.S.2011, § 2367(3).
Once the affiliated group elects to file a consolidated Oklahoma income tax return, the election is
binding and will continue for future years unless the Tax Commission releases the affiliated group
from the requirement. 68 O.S.2011, § 2367(3). If an affiliated group elects to file a consolidated
Oklahoma income tax return, the group’s consolidated income, loss or deductions shall be
determined on a “component member by component member basis” according to Sections 2358
and 2362 of Title 68. Id; See also OAC 710:50-17-31 and OAC 710:50-17-34.
17. The administrative rule on filing a consolidated Oklahoma return in effect during
the 2017 tax year at issue provides:
710:50-17-31. Filing a consolidated Oklahoma return
(a) In filing a Consolidated Income Tax Return for Oklahoma, the
Oklahoma taxable income for each corporation is computed separately on
its own factors and then combined for one total income upon which the tax
is computed.

(b) A Consolidated Oklahoma Income Tax Return is generally
recognized as a combined return.
(c) A corporation's election to file a separate return or consolidated
return is made with the timely filing of the return. Once the election is
made, it is irrevocable for all future tax years unless the Oklahoma Tax
Commission releases the affiliated group of corporations from such
election.
(d) When an election is made to file an Oklahoma Combined Return the
following criteria must be met.
(1) A federal consolidated returns must have been filed.
(2) All companies doing business in Oklahoma must be
included in the Oklahoma Combination.
(3) Only those corporations included in the federal consolidation
may be included in the Oklahoma combined return.
(4) The Parent Corporation name should be used for the
Oklahoma return and all corporations must be included in one filing.
Returns belonging to a Oklahoma Combination will not be accepted if
mailed in separately. [See: 68 O.S. §2367]
OAC 710:50-17-31.
18. The administrative rule regarding computation of taxable income on consolidated
returns in effect during the 2017 tax year at issue provides, in pertinent part:
710:50-17-34. Computation of Oklahoma taxable income on
consolidated return
(a) To arrive at Oklahoma taxable income on a Consolidated Return, the
group's consolidated income, loss or deductions shall be determined in
accordance with the provisions of 68 O.S. § 2358 and 68 O.S. 2362.
Therefore, each member of the group shall determine its Oklahoma net
taxable income by whatever method is proper (direct accounting, unitary,
etc.) and then, the net taxable income of each member shall be aggregated
into a taxable total.
Example: The Federal Net Income reported for the following groups of
corporations was as follows:
Corporation A $10,000.00
Corporation B 5,000.00
Corporation C (14,000.00)
Corporation D 1,000.00
Corporation E 6,000.00
Consolidated Federal Net Income $8,000.00
Assume only corporations (A), (B) and (C) operate in Oklahoma. Also
assume corporation (A) and (C) are unitary business[es] while corporation
(B) is not of a unitary nature and is on direct accounting. If, in this example,
Oklahoma's portion, using the three factor formula, was 10% and 5% for

19. Net operating loss deduction as an adjustment in arriving at Oklahoma Taxable
Income is found in 68 O.S.Supp.2016, § 2358(A)(3). Section 2358(A)(3) provides, in part:
A. The taxable income of any taxpayer shall be adjusted to arrive at Oklahoma
taxable income for corporations and Oklahoma adjusted gross income for
individuals, as follows:
* * *
3. The amount of any federal net operating loss deduction shall be adjusted as
follows:
* * *
b. For carryovers and carrybacks to taxable years beginning after December 31,
1980, the amount of any net operating loss deduction allowed for the taxable year
shall be an amount equal to the aggregate of the Oklahoma net operating loss
carryovers and carrybacks to such year. Oklahoma net operating losses shall be
separately determined by reference to Section 172 of the Internal Revenue Code,
26 U.S.C., Section 172, as modified by the Oklahoma Income Tax Act, Section
2351 et seq. of this title, and shall be allowed without regard to the existence of a
federal net operating loss. For tax years beginning after December 31, 2000, and
ending before January 1, 2008, the years to which such losses may be carried shall
be determined solely by reference to Section 172 of the Internal Revenue Code,
26 U.S.C., Section 172, with the exception that the terms "net operating loss" and
"taxable income" shall be replaced with "Oklahoma net operating loss" and
"Oklahoma taxable income". For tax years beginning after December 31, 2007,
and ending before January 1, 2009, years to which such losses may be carried back
shall be limited to two (2) years. For tax years beginning after December 31, 2008,
the years to which such losses may be carried back shall be determined solely by
reference to Section 172 of the Internal Revenue Code, 26 U.S.C., Section 172,
with the exception that the terms "net operating loss" and "taxable income" shall
be replaced with "Oklahoma net operating loss" and "Oklahoma taxable income".
* * *
68 O.S.Supp.2016, § 2358(A)(3); See also OAC 710:50-17-51(4).

20. The relevant portion of 26 U.S.C.A. § 172 (West 2014) in effect for the 2017 tax
year, states in pertinent part:
(a) Deduction allowed
There shall be allowed as a deduction for the taxable year an amount equal to
the aggregate of (1) the net operation loss carryovers to such year, plus (2) the
net operating loss carrybacks to such year. For purposes of this subtitle, the
term “net operating loss deduction” means the deduction allowed by this
subsection.
(b) Net operating loss carrybacks and carryovers
(1) Years to which loss may be carried
(A) General rule
Except as otherwise provided in this paragraph,10 a net operating loss
for any taxable year-
(i) Shall be a net operating loss carryback to each of the 2 taxable years
preceding the taxable year of such loss, and
(ii) Shall be a net operating loss carryover to each of the 20 taxable
years following the taxable year of the loss.
* * *
(c) Net operating loss defined
For purposes of this section, the term “net operating loss” means the excess of
the deductions allowed by this chapter over the gross income. Such excess shall
be computed with the modifications specified in subsection (d).
* * *
26 U.S.C.A. § 172 (West 2014).

23. In Getty Oil Co. v. Okla. Tax Comm’n, 1977 OK 19, ¶ 9, 563 P.2d 627, 630, the
Oklahoma Supreme Court held the net operating loss statute did not intend to create a deduction
but to limit one already reflected on the federal return. The Court addressed the history of the net
11 The remaining part of Treas. Reg. § 1.1502-21-(c)(1) is not at issue in the current proceeding and is therefore not included.
12 of 20 OTC ORDER NO. 2024-06-04-15

NON-PRECEDENTIAL DECISION OKLAHOMA TAX COMMISSION
operating loss statute pointing out prior to 1971, Oklahoma did not allow a net operating loss
carryover from a prior year. Id. at ¶ 2. After Oklahoma adopted the Act, Oklahoma used the IRC
as a base for income tax. Id. The net operating loss statute then allowed carryover from previous
years as allowed for federal income tax purposes but limited the deduction to the Oklahoma net
operating loss portion. Getty, 1977 OK 19, ¶ 2. The version of Section 2358 in effect for the 2017
tax year at issue allows Oklahoma NOLs to be utilized without regard to the existence of a federal
NOL. 68 O.S.Supp.2016, § 2358(A)(3).
24. In State Dep’t of Revenue, v. Coca-Cola Refreshments, U.S.A., Inc., et al., 248
So.3d 18 (Ala. Civ. App. 2017), the Alabama Department of Revenue sought to prevent the

ANALYSIS
In this case of first impression, the parties stipulated the issue to be decided is “[w]hether
the Division properly disallowed Protestant’s use of Oklahoma net operating losses generated by
AFFILIATED COMPANY during the 2015 and 2016 tax years as claimed on Protestant’s 2017
Form 512 Corporation Income Tax Return?” The amount of the NOLs is not in controversy.
Neither party contends the NOLs were not properly generated and claimed by AFFILIATED
COMPANY on its 2015 and 2016 separate Oklahoma corporate income tax returns. The point of
contention between the parties is the use of the 2015 and 2016 NOLs on the consolidated 2017
Return because AFFILIATED COMPANY filed separate Oklahoma corporate income tax returns
for the 2015 and 2016 loss years.
Additional pertinent facts show AFFILIATED COMPANY was a member of Protestant’s
affiliated group every day of the year for 2015, 2016, and 2017. Protestant filed consolidated
federal corporate income tax returns for 2015, 2016, and 2017 on behalf of the affiliated group of
corporations. Protestant elected to file a consolidated Oklahoma corporate income tax return for
the first time in 2017 on behalf of the affiliated group of corporations. The 2017 Return included
net operating loss carryover deductions for Oklahoma net operating losses generated by
AFFILIATED COMPANY for 2015 and 2016 totaling $954,163. AFFILIATED COMPANY
separately computed its taxable income on its own factors on the 2017 Return. The Division has
not received notice the IRS adjusted Protestant’s taxable income on its 2017 federal consolidated
corporate income tax return.
Net operating loss deduction is authorized under the Act as an adjustment to federal taxable
income to arrive at Oklahoma taxable income pursuant to 68 O.S.Supp.2016, § 2358(A)(3). In
1977, the Oklahoma Supreme Court in Getty, supra, covered the history of the NOL deduction. At
the time of Getty, NOL deduction allowed for Oklahoma income tax purposes was limited to the
Oklahoma portion of NOLs reflected on the federal return. After Getty, Section 2358 was amended
and allowed NOL deduction without regard to a federal NOL using IRC § 172 as a guide but still
limited to the Oklahoma portion of the loss. Both Section 2358(A)(3) and OKLAHOMA
ADMINISTRATIVE CODE 710:50-17-51(4)(A)(3) in effect for the 2017 income tax year provide
NOLs may be carried over until utilized without regard to a federal loss. Section 2358(A)(3) does
not limit an NOL deduction other than to limit the deduction to the Oklahoma portion of the losses
and refers to IRC § 172 for determination of the years to which losses may be carried.
Oklahoma statute 68 O.S.2011, § 2367 provides the authority for an affiliated group of
corporations to file a consolidated Oklahoma income tax return under certain circumstances. Under
subsection (2), Protestant is permitted to file a consolidated Oklahoma income tax return since it
filed a consolidated federal income tax return pursuant to 26 U.S.C. § 1501 (2012), and since one
or more members of the affiliated group of corporations derived a portion of their income from
sources outside of Oklahoma. Under subsection (3), since the election to file an Oklahoma
consolidated corporate income tax return has been made, Protestant is now required to continue
filing a consolidated Oklahoma corporate income tax return each year unless released by the Tax
Commission from the election. Protestant’s consolidated income, loss or deductions shall be
determined on a “component member by component member basis” as required by subsection (3)
and OAC 710:50-17-31.

The starting point for computing Oklahoma taxable corporate income is the taxable income
shown before the NOL and special deduction line of the federal income tax return. AFFILIATED
COMPANY’S total federal taxable income was reported on the affiliated group’s 2017 federal
corporate income tax return. AFFILIATED COMPANY correctly used the amount reported on the
federal return as a starting point and separately computed its Oklahoma taxable income on
Protestant’s 2017 Return. AFFILIATED COMPANY’S separate income was then used together
with the other affiliated members’ separate Oklahoma taxable income to determine the group’s
Oklahoma consolidated income.
The 2017 Oklahoma corporate income tax return Form 512 line 1 instructs taxpayers to
enter their Oklahoma taxable income, if consolidated, from Form 512-TI. Protestant used the total
Oklahoma income from each of its affiliates’ separately calculated Oklahoma income (before NOL
and tax accrual deduction) to arrive at the total Oklahoma income on the 2017 Form 512-TI.
Oklahoma NOL deduction is calculated after each member of an affiliated group separately
calculates their Oklahoma income. OKLAHOMA ADMINISTRATIVE CODE 710:50-17-34, supra,
provides an example of how to determine Oklahoma taxable income on a consolidated return.
Nothing in the facts indicate Protestant incorrectly calculated AFFILIATED COMPANY’S
Oklahoma income.
The Division’s adjustment letter cites three reasons for denying Protestant’s use of
AFFILIATED COMPANY’S NOLs from 2015 and 2016 on its 2017 Return. First, the Division
states AFFILIATED COMPANY’S NOLs for 2015 and 2016 occurred prior to a consolidated
return being filed for the first time in Oklahoma. Second, the Division states the losses can only
be used to the extent AFFILIATED COMPANY had taxable income on the consolidated return
and further states the losses cannot be used to offset income from the rest of the consolidated
group. Third, the Division’s adjustment letter cites IRS Reg. 1.1502-21(c)(1) which limits the use
of NOLs arising from SRLY.
Protestant cited several cases from other jurisdictions in support of its argument the
Division erred in adjusting the 2017 Return. Since this matter is a case of first impression, there is
no Oklahoma authority directly on point. In Coca-Cola, supra, Alabama attempted to limit the
taxpayer’s use of NOL on a consolidated return because the loss was first reported on a separate
return of an affiliated member. The court ultimately sided with the taxpayer in allowing the NOL
on the consolidated Alabama return.
Here, the Division denied Protestant’s use of the NOLs on its 2017 Return because the
losses were first reported on separate returns of an affiliated member, AFFILIATED COMPANY.
Under Section 2358 of the Act, NOLs must be separately determined using IRC § 172 as a guide.
IRS regulation 1.1502-21(c)(1) limits the use of an NOL from a SRLY of a member of an affiliated
group. The only regulatory authority cited in the Division’s adjustment letter, IRS Reg. 1.1502-
21(c)(1), does not apply to Protestant. The parties stipulated Protestant was a member of the
affiliated group of corporations every day of the year for 2015, 2016, and 2017. IRS Reg. 1.1502-
1(f)(2)(ii) states SRLY does not include a “[a] separate return year of any corporation which was
a member of the group for each day of such year.”

Protestant cited Tax Commission Letter Ruling LR-06-201 as further support for its
position arguing the facts in LR-06-201 are virtually identical to the facts in this case. The Tax
Commission responded in LR-06-201 that the NOLs generated by an affiliated member on a
separately filed Oklahoma return from a prior year could be used to offset income on a consolidated
return. Protestant may not rely on LR-06-201, however, the other authorities cited by Protestant
are persuasive. In this case, Protestant elected to file a consolidated return. Each affiliated member
separately calculated their income, losses, and deductions on the consolidated return. Oklahoma
Form 512-TI provides for NOL deduction after the total income of the affiliated group’s Oklahoma
income is computed.
There is nothing cited in statute, rule, or caselaw that limits the NOL deduction for the
reasons stated by the Division. The Division argues LR-06-201 is consistent with its “policy and
position” on its treatment of other taxpayers but cites no authority for the denial of the use of the
NOL deduction on a consolidated return based upon the facts of this case. The Division may not
limit the parameters of a statute with an unpromulgated rule without violating the Administrative
Procedures Act.
The Division argues in its response brief that Protestant cannot utilize the NOL deduction
since it did not utilize the deduction on its 2017 consolidated federal return. The Division’s
argument is contrary to 68 O.S.Supp.2016, § 2358. Section 2358(A)(3)(b) specifically states
“Oklahoma net operating losses shall be separately determined by reference to Section 172 of the
Internal Revenue Code, 26 U.S.C., Section 172, as modified by the Oklahoma Income Tax Act,
Section 2351 et seq. of this title, and shall be allowed without regard to the existence of a federal
net operating loss.”
The undersigned concludes an Oklahoma NOL deduction from a separately filed
Oklahoma corporate income tax return from a prior year of a member of an affiliated group of
corporations (who was a member of the affiliated group for every day of the loss year) may be
used on a consolidated Oklahoma corporate income tax return as long as all other statutory
requirements are met and followed.
RECOMMENDATION
Based on the foregoing, it is recommended the protest to the adjustment of
Protestant’s 2017 Consolidated Oklahoma Corporation Income Tax Return be sustained.
